1: ---
     2: # Deploy a Windows 11 desktop test host for interactive / computer-use agent
     3: # testing, with OpenAI Codex installed by default.
     4: #
     5: # WHAT IT DOES
     6: #   Clones the generalized win11 golden (SSP DataSource `win11` in
     7: #   openshift-virtualization-os-images) into a running KubeVirt VirtualMachine
     8: #   on api.ocp.igou.systems, drives Windows OOBE with a sysprep specialization
     9: #   unattend (local-admin mode, WinRM-over-HTTPS listener), exposes WinRM (5986)
    10: #   and RDP (3389) via NodePort Services, then provisions the guest over psrp:
    11: #   an execution-policy guard, power hardening (idle standby/hibernation off —
    12: #   a sleeping guest drops RDP/WinRM/guest-agent while the VMI still shows
    13: #   Ready), a debloat pass (bloatware Appx, consumer content/nags, OneDrive), a
    14: #   Chocolatey app set (PowerShell 7 + git + nodejs-lts + python + Firefox +
    15: #   Chrome + the Codex CLI), Firefox as default browser, the Codex/ChatGPT
    16: #   desktop app, optional direct MSI installers, and Remote Desktop. An operator then RDPs in to complete the
    17: #   one-time, MANDATORY interactive Codex sign-in (ChatGPT OAuth — no headless
    18: #   path exists for the app; the CLI supports OPENAI_API_KEY auth).
    19: #
    20: #   Codex desktop app packaging: the GUI app is MSIX/Store-distributed
    21: #   (product id 9PLM9XGG6VKS) and a Store session cannot be driven over WinRM,
    22: #   but since 2026-03 OpenAI publishes the Store-signed offline package +
    23: #   license for enterprise deployment (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/
    24: #   windows-deployment), so this playbook provisions it machine-wide with
    25: #   Add-AppxProvisionedPackage — it registers into each user profile at that
    26: #   user's next logon.
    27: #
    28: #   Fleet-parity additions (devenv-host treatment for this VM):
    29: #   * Metrics: node_exporter has NO Windows build and the prometheus.prometheus
    30: #     collection ships Linux-only roles, so the guest runs the supported
    31: #     equivalent — prometheus-community/windows_exporter — installed through
    32: #     the chocolatey.chocolatey collection (service windows_exporter, :9182),
    33: #     firewall opened, plus a ClusterIP `<vm>-metrics` Service so in-cluster
    34: #     Prometheus (UWM) can scrape it.
    35: #   * T3 Code: the `t3` npm package, pinned to the same version igou-devenv
    36: #     pins in mise.toml. Its native dep node-pty ships win32-x64 prebuilds in
    37: #     the npm tarball, so no MSVC toolchain is needed in the guest. `t3 serve`
    38: #     runs always-on (hidden boot scheduled task, loopback bind) fronted by
    39: #     tailnet HTTPS via tailscale serve, so the t3 desktop app can use the VM
    40: #     as a remote environment at https://<vm>.<tailnet>.ts.net.
    41: #   * Tailnet: `tailscale up --unattended` with the tailscale-oauth-codex
    42: #     OAuth client secret (1P lab_external_api_keys, resolved lazily on the
    43: #     controller/EE — the secret never lands on the guest disk). Joins
    44: #     advertise designated tags; the tailnet ACL must let the OAuth client
    45: #     own each tag (same contract as playbooks/tailscale/tailscale.yml).
    46: #
    47: # CLIENT-SKU / sysprep gotchas baked in (do not "simplify" away):
    48: #   * Win11 client SKUs DISABLE the built-in Administrator, so the unattend runs
    49: #     in local_account mode: it creates windows_desktop_admin_user as a local
    50: #     admin and sets LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy=1 (without it psrp/WinRM auth
    51: #     succeeds but every privileged op 401s / access-denies).
    52: #   * The sysprep volume references the Secret as `secret: {name: ...}`. The key
    53: #     is `name`, NOT `secretName` — `secretName` is silently dropped by the API
    54: #     and the VMI wedges Pending.
    55: #   * preference windows.11 requires >=2 vCPU: u1.large works, u1.medium is
    56: #     webhook-rejected (422). windows.11 already injects EFI+secureBoot firmware
    57: #     and the vTPM requirement, so no hand-rolled firmware/tpm block is needed
    58: #     (non-persistent vTPM is fine for eval clones).
    59: #   * Fresh KubeVirt NICs classify as the Public network profile, so the WinRM
    60: #     (in the unattend) and RDP firewall rules cover ALL profiles.
    61: #   * Chocolatey's bootstrap runs a downloaded .ps1 which the client-SKU default
    62: #     execution policy (Restricted) blocks, so the guard sets LocalMachine to
    63: #     RemoteSigned first.
    64: #
    65: # ROLE DECOMPOSITION
    66: #   The in-guest provisioning tasks now live in four reusable roles (each with
    67: #   its own meta/argument_specs.yml + molecule scenario), imported below with
    68: #   the windows_desktop_* knobs mapped onto each role's inputs:
    69: #     * windows_power        - idle standby / hibernation off
    70: #     * windows_debloat      - bloatware Appx, consumer content/nags, OneDrive
    71: #     * windows_computer_use - autologon, never-lock/blank, quiet UAC, toasts
    72: #                              off, logon resolution pin
    73: #     * windows_desktop_apps - execution-policy guard + Chocolatey + MSI +
    74: #                              Firefox default (the guard MUST run before any
    75: #                              Chocolatey work, so this role owns it)
    76: #   The cluster-side provisioning, guest MTU clamp, Codex desktop app, Remote
    77: #   Desktop, and verification tasks stay in this playbook.
    78: #
    79: # VARIABLES (all prefixed windows_desktop_):
    80: #   windows_desktop_name            - VM / Secret / Service base name (default codex-desktop)
    81: #   windows_desktop_namespace       - target namespace (default windows-images)
    82: #   windows_desktop_state           - present (default) | absent. absent tears
    83: #                                     down the VM, its boot DataVolume, both
    84: #                                     NodePort Services, and the sysprep Secret.
    85: #   windows_desktop_admin_user      - local admin created by the unattend AND the
    86: #                                     psrp connect user (default igou)
    87: #   windows_desktop_admin_password  - REQUIRED, no default. Source:

    89: #   windows_desktop_datasource_name       - golden DataSource (default win11)

    15:     - name: confirm_upgrade
    16:       prompt: |
    17: 
    18:         ===================================================================================
    19:         Are you sure you want to rollback a PostgreSQL upgrade?
    20: 
    21:         This can only be done if the v{{ new_version }} cluster has not been started yet.
    22:         ===================================================================================
    23:         Respond with [y/N]
    24:       private: no

    33:         that: new_version_service not in ansible_facts.services or ansible_facts.services.get(new_version_service).state == 'stopped'
    34:         msg: "{{ new_version_service }} is running. Rollback is not possible."

    36:     - name: Check upgrade in progress
    37:       become: yes
    38:       stat:
    39:         path: "/opt/data/postgresql/{{ old_version }}/main/global/pg_control.old"

    11: #   PROVIDER_BIN    path to complyctl-provider-openscap   (default: ~/.complytime/providers/...)

    15: - name: Set up complyctl NIST scanner on RHEL9

    18:   vars:

    29:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    30:     # complyctl binary
    31:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    32:     - name: Copy complyctl binary
    33:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    34:         src: "{{ complyctl_bin }}"

    41:       changed_when: false

    43:     - name: Show complyctl version

    45:         msg: "{{ ver.stdout }}"
    46: 
    47:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48:     # complyctl-provider-openscap
    49:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    50:     - name: Create provider directory

    52:         path: /root/.local/share/complytime/providers

    60:         mode: "0755"
    61: 
    62:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    63:     # OCI registry — distribution/distribution binary (no podman required).
    64:     # Runs as a systemd service inside the VM listening on all interfaces.
    65:     # The host pushes bundles to ansible_host:{{ registry_port }} via oras;
    66:     # complyctl on the VM uses http://localhost:{{ registry_port }}.
    67:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    68:     - name: Check if registry binary is already installed
    69:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    70:         path: /usr/local/bin/registry
    71:       register: registry_bin_stat
    72: 
    73:     - name: Download distribution/distribution registry binary
    74:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
    75:         curl -sL \
    76:           "https://github.com/distribution/distribution/releases/download/v2.8.3/registry_2.8.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz" \
    77:           | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin registry
    78:         chmod +x /usr/local/bin/registry
    79:       when: not registry_bin_stat.stat.exists
    80: 
    81:     - name: Create registry storage directory
    82:       ansible.builtin.file:
    83:         path: /var/lib/gemara-registry
    84:         state: directory
    85:         mode: "0755"
    86: 
    87:     - name: Write registry config
    88:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    89:         dest: /etc/gemara-registry.yml
    90:         mode: "0644"
    91:         content: |
    92:           version: 0.1
    93:           log:
    94:             level: warn
    95:           storage:
    96:             filesystem:
    97:               rootdirectory: /var/lib/gemara-registry
    98:             delete:
    99:               enabled: true
   100:           http:
   101:             addr: :{{ registry_port }}
   102: 
   103:     - name: Create systemd service for registry
   104:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   105:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/gemara-registry.service
   106:         mode: "0644"
   107:         content: |
   108:           [Unit]
   109:           Description=Gemara OCI Registry
   110:           After=network.target
   111:           [Service]
   112:           ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/registry serve /etc/gemara-registry.yml
   113:           Restart=always
   114:           RestartSec=3
   115:           [Install]
   116:           WantedBy=multi-user.target
   117: 
   118:     - name: Enable and start registry service
   119:       ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   120:         name: gemara-registry
   121:         state: started
   122:         enabled: true
   123:         daemon_reload: true
   124: 
   125:     - name: Wait for registry to become ready
   126:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   127:         url: "http://localhost:{{ registry_port }}/v2/"
   128:         status_code: 200
   129:       retries: 15
   130:       delay: 2
   131:       register: registry_ready
   132:       until: registry_ready.status == 200
   133: 
   134:     - name: Registry is ready
   135:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   136:         msg: "OCI registry running at localhost:{{ registry_port }} (and {{ ansible_host }}:{{ registry_port }} from the host)"
   137: 
   138:     - name: Open registry port in the VM firewall
   139:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
   140:         firewall-cmd --add-port={{ registry_port }}/tcp --permanent
   141:         firewall-cmd --reload
   142:       args:
   143:         executable: /bin/bash
   144:       changed_when: true
   145: 
   146:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147:     # SCAP data stream — always copy the repo-built version.
   148:     # The system RPM (scap-security-guide) predates the nist_800_53 profile
   149:     # commit and will not contain that profile.  The built data stream must
   150:     # be deployed even if the RPM is already installed.
   151:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   152:     - name: "Copy built data stream from host"
   153:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   154:         src: "{{ repo_root }}/build/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml"
   155:         dest: "{{ ds_dest }}"
   156:         mode: "0644"
   157:         force: true
   158: 
   159:     - name: Confirm data stream has nist_800_53 profile
   160:       ansible.builtin.command: "grep -c nist_800_53 {{ ds_dest }}"
   161:       register: profile_check
   162:       changed_when: false
   163:       failed_when: profile_check.rc != 0 or profile_check.stdout | int == 0
   164: 
   165:     - name: Show data stream status
   166:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   167:         msg: "Data stream: {{ ds_dest }} — nist_800_53 profile present ({{ profile_check.stdout }} occurrences)"
   168: 
   169:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   170:     # Summary
   171:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   172:     - name: Setup complete
   173:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   174:         msg: |
   175:           VM is ready. Run the scan with:
   176:             ansible-playbook -i ansible/inventory.ini ansible/scan.yml

name: src/clawrium/platform/shell/shell_macos.yaml
review_question: Does this playbook combine unrelated responsibility domains so strongly that it should be decomposed?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # macOS counterpart to shell.yaml. Same shape: run an arbitrary command
     3: # on the host as the agent's unix user in a login bash shell
     4: # (`/bin/bash -lc '<cmd>'`), capturing stdout/stderr/rc via three
     5: # base64-tagged debug events (SHELL_STDOUT=, SHELL_STDERR=, SHELL_RC=).
     6: #
     7: # Kill window is enforced via Homebrew's `gtimeout` (coreutils) when
     8: # available. macOS ships no `/usr/bin/timeout`; without `gtimeout` we
     9: # fall back to running `bash -lc` directly and rely on the
    10: # ansible-runner outer timeout (`effective + _RUNNER_GRACE_S` in
    11: # core/agent_shell.py) as the kill backstop. The cost of the fallback
    12: # is a wider kill window (+25s); the user-facing rc=124 contract is
    13: # unchanged because runner status `timeout` already maps to rc=124 in
    14: # core.
    15: - hosts: all
    16:   gather_facts: false
    17:   tasks:
    18:     # No OS-family guard here: gather_facts is off (latency matters),
    19:     # so `ansible_os_family` would be undefined. The dispatcher in
    20:     # core/playbook_resolver.py is the routing source of truth.
    21: 
    22:     - name: Validate agent_name (defense-in-depth)
    23:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    24:         msg: "Invalid agent_name"
    25:       when:
    26:         - agent_name is not match('^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$')
    27: 
    28:     - name: Validate cmd_b64 is defined and non-empty
    29:       # If `cmd_b64` is missing or empty the inline `b64decode` filter
    30:       # in the command task would emit a confusing Jinja error
    31:       # silenced by `no_log: true` (mirrors shell.yaml #761 iter-3 W3).
    32:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    33:         msg: "cmd_b64 must be a non-empty base64 string"
    34:       when:
    35:         - (cmd_b64 is not defined) or (cmd_b64 | length == 0)
    36: 
    37:     - name: Validate shell_timeout is a positive integer
    38:       # Without this guard, `{{ shell_timeout | int }}` silently
    39:       # becomes `0`, which `gtimeout` interprets as "no kill window".
    40:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    41:         msg: "shell_timeout must be a positive integer (got {{ shell_timeout | default('undefined') }})"
    42:       when:
    43:         - (shell_timeout is not defined) or (shell_timeout | int < 1)
    44: 
    45:     - name: Discover gtimeout (coreutils) as agent user
    46:       # Include `/opt/local/bin` so MacPorts installs are picked up
    47:       # alongside Homebrew arm64 (`/opt/homebrew/bin`) and x86_64
    48:       # (`/usr/local/bin`). `failed_when: false` (idiomatic Ansible)
    49:       # is the no-fail mechanism; `|| true` would be redundant.
    50:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
    51:         PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/opt/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin which gtimeout
    52:       args:
    53:         executable: /bin/bash
    54:       become: true
    55:       become_user: "{{ agent_name }}"
    56:       register: gtimeout_which
    57:       changed_when: false
    58:       failed_when: false
    59: 
    60:     - name: Resolve gtimeout binary
    61:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    62:         resolved_gtimeout: "{{ gtimeout_which.stdout | default('') | trim }}"
    63: 
    64:     - name: Run command in login shell as agent user (with gtimeout)
    65:       # gtimeout enforces the kill window so the remote process is
    66:       # reaped even if ansible-runner is killed. `--kill-after=5`
    67:       # follows SIGTERM with SIGKILL 5s later if the process ignores
    68:       # TERM. Same `bash -lc` semantics + `cmd_b64 | b64decode` hop as
    69:       # shell.yaml so the user-supplied command never passes through
    70:       # Ansible's recursive Jinja templater.
    71:       ansible.builtin.command:
    72:         argv:
    73:           - "{{ resolved_gtimeout }}"
    74:           - "--kill-after=5"
    75:           - "{{ shell_timeout | int }}"
    76:           - /bin/bash
    77:           - -lc
    78:           - "{{ cmd_b64 | b64decode }}"
    79:       become: true
    80:       become_user: "{{ agent_name }}"
    81:       register: shell_result
    82:       failed_when: false
    83:       changed_when: false
    84:       no_log: true
    85:       when: (resolved_gtimeout | length) > 0
    86: 
    87:     - name: Run command in login shell as agent user (no gtimeout)
    88:       # Fallback when coreutils is not installed on the macOS host.
    89:       # ansible-runner's outer timeout (`effective + _RUNNER_GRACE_S`)
    90:       # is the kill backstop; status `timeout` already maps to rc=124
    91:       # in core/agent_shell.py.
    92:       ansible.builtin.command:
    93:         argv:
    94:           - /bin/bash
    95:           - -lc
    96:           - "{{ cmd_b64 | b64decode }}"
    97:       become: true
    98:       become_user: "{{ agent_name }}"
    99:       register: shell_result_fallback
   100:       failed_when: false
   101:       changed_when: false
   102:       no_log: true
   103:       when: (resolved_gtimeout | length) == 0
   104: 
   105:     - name: Merge run-task result
   106:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   107:         shell_result: "{{ shell_result_fallback if ((resolved_gtimeout | length) == 0) else shell_result }}"
   108: 
   109:     - name: Emit stdout
   110:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   111:         msg: "SHELL_STDOUT={{ shell_result.stdout | default('') | b64encode }}"
   112: 
   113:     - name: Emit stderr
   114:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   115:         msg: "SHELL_STDERR={{ shell_result.stderr | default('') | b64encode }}"
   116: 
   117:     - name: Emit rc
   118:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   119:         msg: "SHELL_RC={{ shell_result.rc | default(255) }}"

name: playbooks/truenas/publish_windows_isos.yml
review_question: Does this playbook combine unrelated responsibility domains so strongly that it should be decomposed?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Publish the Microsoft Evaluation Center Windows ISO library on
     3: # public.igou.systems AND emit no-prompt (remastered) siblings for the golden
     4: # pipeline's unattended install feedstock.
     5: #
     6: # Design: igou-io/igou-ansible#343 (Windows golden-image design v3, increment 1);
     7: # publish leg originally from igou-io/igou-openshift#380 Phase 1.
     8: #
     9: # ── Publish leg ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    10: # The nginx-reverse-proxy container on TrueNAS serves /mnt/ssd/public read-only
    11: # at public.igou.systems (autoindex), so the ISOs under
    12: # /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/ are published with zero nginx config changes:
    13: #   https://public.igou.systems/isos/windows/<file>.iso   (and http:// for CDI)
    14: #
    15: # ASSUMPTION (not a task): the vanilla eval ISO library and its SHA256SUMS
    16: # already live at /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/ on TrueNAS. This play does NOT
    17: # transfer anything — it only asserts presence + integrity of the serving copy.
    18: # igounas (Synology) remains the archival provenance of the media, but that is
    19: # background, not a runtime dependency: no igounas connectivity is needed here.
    20: #
    21: # One-time seed procedure for adding a NEW eval ISO to the library (run by hand
    22: # ON TrueNAS, then add the file to truenas_windows_isos below):
    23: #   1. Copy the ISO into the served dir. igounas DSM has no sftp/scp, so stream
    24: #      it over ssh (cat) from TrueNAS:
    25: #        ssh igou@igounas.igou.systems \
    26: #          "cat /volume1/igoushare/Lab/isos/windows/<file>.iso" \
    27: #          > /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/<file>.iso
    28: #   2. Append the upstream checksum line to the manifest:
    29: #        echo "<sha256>  <file>.iso" >> /mnt/ssd/public/isos/windows/SHA256SUMS
    30: # Thereafter this play verifies it on every run.
    31: #
    32: # ── Remaster leg (why noprompt media exists) ───────────────────────────────
    33: # Windows install media stops at a "Press any key to boot from CD…" prompt.
    34: # For a fully declarative KubeVirt build the firmware must NOT wait: with a
    35: # no-keypress firmware the prompting cdboot.efi makes the firmware SKIP the CD
    36: # and boot-loop a blank disk. Microsoft ships (undocumented) efisys_noprompt.bin
    37: # / cdboot_noprompt.efi variants; swapping them in and repacking the ISO yields
    38: # media that boots straight into Setup. This is the only declarative path
    39: # (matches Red Hat's pipeline) — see #343 review. TrueNAS SCALE has no native
    40: # xorriso, so the whole remaster runs inside a throwaway pinned docker container
    41: # that has /isos bind-mounted.
    42: #
    43: # This playbook runs fine from the devcontainer: the only network path it needs
    44: # is devcontainer → truenas SSH (truenas_admin@truenas.igou.systems).
    45: 
    46: - name: Publish Windows eval ISOs on public.igou.systems
    47:   hosts: truenas
    48:   gather_facts: false
    49:   become: false
    50:   vars:
    51:     # Serving location on TrueNAS; override in group_vars/truenas.yml as needed.
    52:     truenas_public_pool: ssd
    53:     # Refquota bump is OPT-IN: the live ssd/public dataset deliberately runs
    54:     # refquota=none (pool has ample headroom). Set a BYTE COUNT (int, e.g.
    55:     # 161061273600 for 150GiB) to enforce one; empty skips the task.
    56:     truenas_public_quota: ""
    57:     truenas_windows_isos:
    58:       - winserver2025-eval-en-us.iso
    59:       - winserver2022-eval-en-us.iso
    60:       - winserver2019-eval-en-us.iso
    61:       - winserver2016-eval-en-us.iso
    62:       - win11-25h2-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
    63:       - win11-ltsc2024-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
    64:       - win11-iot-ltsc2024-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
    65:     _dst_dir: "/mnt/{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public/isos/windows"
    66:   tasks:
    67: 
    68:     - name: Bump the public dataset refquota (headroom for the ISO library)
    69:       # arensb.truenas.filesystem takes refquota as an integer byte count.
    70:       when: truenas_public_quota | string | length > 0
    71:       arensb.truenas.filesystem:
    72:         name: "{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public"
    73:         state: present
    74:         type: FILESYSTEM
    75:         refquota: "{{ truenas_public_quota | int }}"
    76:       tags: [quota]
    77: 
    78:     - name: Ensure the published ISO directory exists
    79:       ansible.builtin.file:
    80:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}"
    81:         state: directory
    82:         mode: "0755"
    83:       tags: [dir]
    84: 
    85:     - name: Stat each published ISO
    86:       # Presence of the vanilla library is an assumption, not a task — assert it.
    87:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    88:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item }}"
    89:       register: _iso_stat
    90:       loop: "{{ truenas_windows_isos }}"
    91:       loop_control:
    92:         label: "{{ item }}"
    93:       tags: [verify]
    94: 
    95:     - name: Assert every listed ISO is present in the serving directory
    96:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    97:         that: item.stat.exists
    98:         fail_msg: >-
    99:           {{ item.item }} is missing from {{ _dst_dir }}. This play assumes the
   100:           vanilla ISO library is already seeded there; add it via the one-time
   101:           seed procedure documented in this file's header (stream from igounas
   102:           over ssh cat, then append its line to SHA256SUMS).
   103:       loop: "{{ _iso_stat.results }}"
   104:       loop_control:
   105:         label: "{{ item.item }}"
   106:       tags: [verify]
   107: 
   108:     - name: Read the SHA256SUMS manifest
   109:       # Slurp once and parse in Jinja (the house idiom — Play 2 slurps its
   110:       # markers) instead of spawning a grep per ISO. A missing manifest fails
   111:       # here, loudly, before the presence assertion below.
   112:       ansible.builtin.slurp:
   113:         src: "{{ _dst_dir }}/SHA256SUMS"
   114:       register: _sums_raw
   115:       tags: [verify]
   116: 
   117:     - name: Assert every listed ISO has a line in SHA256SUMS
   118:       # `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` (below) passes SILENTLY for files that have no
   119:       # line in the manifest, so this explicit presence check is required: an ISO
   120:       # missing from the manifest must fail loudly. Strip the "<hash>  " prefix
   121:       # from each manifest line to get the filename list, then assert membership.
   122:       vars:
   123:         _sums_files: >-
   124:           {{ (_sums_raw.content | b64decode).splitlines()
   125:              | map('regex_replace', '^[0-9A-Fa-f]+ +', '')
   126:              | map('trim') | select | list }}
   127:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   128:         that: item in _sums_files
   129:         fail_msg: >-
   130:           {{ item }} has no line in {{ _dst_dir }}/SHA256SUMS. This play assumes
   131:           the vanilla ISO library is already seeded there; add its checksum line
   132:           via the one-time seed procedure documented in this file's header
   133:           (append "<sha256>  {{ item }}" to SHA256SUMS).
   134:       loop: "{{ truenas_windows_isos }}"
   135:       loop_control:
   136:         label: "{{ item }}"
   137:       tags: [verify]
   138: 
   139:     - name: Verify checksums on the serving copy (hard gate)
   140:       # DEFENDED command (no native equivalent): this verifies EVERY line of the
   141:       # checksum manifest against the files on disk, including the <base>-noprompt
   142:       # siblings the remaster play (Play 2) appends — filenames that no play var
   143:       # enumerates. A native stat get_checksum comparison could only cover the
   144:       # ISOs listed in truenas_windows_isos and would silently ignore those
   145:       # appended remaster lines; no module verifies an arbitrary checksum-manifest
   146:       # file wholesale. Runs before the remaster play; on a fresh system the
   147:       # -noprompt lines are not yet present (only the pristine ISOs are checked),
   148:       # on a converged system both are present and checked.
   149:       ansible.builtin.command:
   150:         cmd: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
   151:         chdir: "{{ _dst_dir }}"
   152:       register: _sha
   153:       changed_when: false
   154:       failed_when: _sha.rc != 0
   155:       tags: [verify]
   156: 
   157: # ── Remaster leg ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   158: # become: true because docker requires root on TrueNAS SCALE (matches the docker
   159: # tasks in configure_docker_containers.yml). Extraction/repack happen in a pinned
   160: # throwaway container; only the idempotence decision, marker write, checksum and
   161: # SHA256SUMS update happen on the host (per #343: lineinfile, hash on host).
   162: 
   163: - name: Emit no-prompt remastered Windows ISOs
   164:   hosts: truenas
   165:   gather_facts: false
   166:   become: true
   167:   vars:
   168:     truenas_public_pool: ssd
   169:     # The two standing golden-pipeline editions. The other 5 remain publishable
   170:     # (above) but unremastered by default; add to this list to remaster them.
   171:     windows_iso_remaster:
   172:       - winserver2025-eval-en-us.iso
   173:       - win11-25h2-enterprise-eval-en-us.iso
   174:     _dst_dir: "/mnt/{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public/isos/windows"
   175:     # Scratch on the same dataset as the ISOs (plenty of space); cleaned up after.
   176:     _scratch: "/mnt/{{ truenas_public_pool }}/public/isos/windows/.remaster-work"
   177:     # Pinned by digest (skopeo-resolved alpine:3.20, 2026-07-11); xorriso via apk.
   178:     # Digest pin makes the remaster reproducible and supply-chain-auditable.
   179:     _remaster_image: >-
   180:       docker.io/library/alpine:3.20@sha256:d9e853e87e55526f6b2917df91a2115c36dd7c696a35be12163d44e6e2a4b6bc
   181:     # The full remaster, run inside the container. $1 = base ISO filename.
   182:     #   1. extract the ISO tree WITHOUT loop-mounting (unprivileged-friendly)
   183:     #   2. preflight (MUST): hard-fail unless BOTH noprompt boot files exist
   184:     #   3. swap the prompting boot files for the noprompt variants
   185:     #   4. repack with the verified official flags (-iso-level 4 packs the >4GB
   186:     #      install.wim; do NOT add -udf)
   187:     _remaster_script: |
   188:       set -eu
   189:       # 7zip reads the UDF tree (where Windows media stores everything but a
   190:       # stub README in ISO9660 — xorriso -osirrox extracts only that ISO9660
   191:       # view and misses efi/, sources/install.wim, boot/); xorriso does the
   192:       # bootable repack. Both are unprivileged, no loop mount, no KVM.
   193:       apk add --no-cache 7zip xorriso >/dev/null
   194:       base="$1"
   195:       src="/isos/${base}"
   196:       tree="/work/${base%.iso}"
   197:       rm -rf "$tree"
   198:       mkdir -p "$tree"
   199:       7z x -bd -bso0 -bsp0 -o"$tree" "$src"
   200:       bootdir="$tree/efi/microsoft/boot"
   201:       # Per-ISO preflight: some media lack the shipped-but-undocumented noprompt
   202:       # boot files. Refuse to produce a silently-still-prompting ISO.
   203:       if [ ! -f "$bootdir/efisys_noprompt.bin" ] || [ ! -f "$bootdir/cdboot_noprompt.efi" ]; then
   204:         echo "PREFLIGHT_FAIL: ${base} lacks efisys_noprompt.bin and/or cdboot_noprompt.efi" >&2
   205:         exit 3
   206:       fi
   207:       rm -f "$bootdir/efisys.bin" "$bootdir/cdboot.efi"
   208:       mv "$bootdir/efisys_noprompt.bin" "$bootdir/efisys.bin"
   209:       mv "$bootdir/cdboot_noprompt.efi" "$bootdir/cdboot.efi"
   210:       xorriso -as mkisofs -no-emul-boot -e "efi/microsoft/boot/efisys.bin" \
   211:         -boot-load-size 1 -iso-level 4 -J -l -D -N -joliet-long \
   212:         -relaxed-filenames -V "WINDOWS" \
   213:         -o "/isos/${base%.iso}-noprompt.iso" "$tree"
   214:       rm -rf "$tree"
   215:       echo "REMASTERED ${base}"
   216:   tasks:
   217: 
   218:     - name: Stat published source ISOs (with sha256)
   219:       # Hashing the source each run is the cost of true hash-idempotence: the
   220:       # marker below stores this hash so we re-remaster only when it changes.
   221:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   222:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item }}"
   223:         get_checksum: true
   224:         checksum_algorithm: sha256
   225:       register: _remaster_src
   226:       loop: "{{ windows_iso_remaster }}"
   227:       loop_control:
   228:         label: "{{ item }}"
   229:       tags: [remaster]
   230: 
   231:     - name: Fail if a remaster source ISO is not published
   232:       ansible.builtin.assert:
   233:         that: item.stat.exists
   234:         fail_msg: "Remaster source {{ item.item }} not present in {{ _dst_dir }} — publish it first."
   235:       loop: "{{ _remaster_src.results }}"
   236:       loop_control:
   237:         label: "{{ item.item }}"
   238:       tags: [remaster]
   239: 
   240:     - name: Read existing source-hash markers
   241:       ansible.builtin.slurp:
   242:         src: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso.src.sha256"
   243:       register: _remaster_marker
   244:       loop: "{{ windows_iso_remaster }}"
   245:       loop_control:
   246:         label: "{{ item }}"
   247:       failed_when: false
   248:       tags: [remaster]
   249: 
   250:     - name: Stat existing no-prompt ISOs
   251:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   252:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   253:       register: _remaster_np
   254:       loop: "{{ windows_iso_remaster }}"
   255:       loop_control:
   256:         label: "{{ item }}"
   257:       tags: [remaster]
   258: 
   259:     - name: Decide which ISOs need remastering (skip when noprompt exists AND marker matches source hash)
   260:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   261:         _to_remaster: >-
   262:           {{ (_to_remaster | default([])) + [item.0.item]
   263:              if ((not item.2.stat.exists)
   264:                   or (item.1.content is not defined)
   265:                   or ((item.1.content | b64decode | trim) != item.0.stat.checksum))
   266:              else (_to_remaster | default([])) }}
   267:       loop: "{{ _remaster_src.results | zip(_remaster_marker.results, _remaster_np.results) | list }}"
   268:       loop_control:
   269:         label: "{{ item.0.item }}"
   270:       tags: [remaster]
   271: 
   272:     - name: Report remaster plan
   273:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   274:         msg: "ISOs to (re)remaster this run: {{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   275:       tags: [remaster]
   276: 
   277:     - name: Create the remaster scratch workspace
   278:       ansible.builtin.file:
   279:         path: "{{ _scratch }}"
   280:         state: directory
   281:         mode: "0700"
   282:       when: (_to_remaster | default([])) | length > 0
   283:       tags: [remaster]
   284: 
   285:     - name: Remaster ISO to no-prompt boot media (extract → preflight → swap → repack)
   286:       # DEFENDED command (over community.docker.docker_container): this is a
   287:       # one-shot `docker run --rm` whose exit code AND stdout ARE the result
   288:       # (changed_when keys on 'REMASTERED', PREFLIGHT_FAIL surfaces via rc/stderr);
   289:       # docker_container manages container lifecycle/state and does not cleanly
   290:       # return a throwaway run's captured output and exit status.
   291:       # argv avoids all shell quoting: the script is passed intact, base as $1.
   292:       # A ~8GB ISO takes a few minutes of IO — hence the generous async window.
   293:       # rc != 0 (e.g. PREFLIGHT_FAIL, exit 3) fails the task with the stderr shown.
   294:       ansible.builtin.command:
   295:         argv:
   296:           - docker
   297:           - run
   298:           - --rm
   299:           - --pull=missing
   300:           - -v
   301:           - "{{ _dst_dir }}:/isos"
   302:           - -v
   303:           - "{{ _scratch }}:/work"
   304:           - "{{ _remaster_image }}"
   305:           - sh
   306:           - -c
   307:           - "{{ _remaster_script }}"
   308:           - remaster
   309:           - "{{ item }}"
   310:       register: _remaster_run
   311:       changed_when: "'REMASTERED' in _remaster_run.stdout"
   312:       # No async: `command` has no default timeout, so it waits out the
   313:       # multi-minute IO on its own. The async wrapper was swallowing the
   314:       # container's stdout/stderr and failing the task with an opaque rc=38.
   315:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   316:       loop_control:
   317:         label: "{{ item }}"
   318:       tags: [remaster]
   319: 
   320:     - name: Record the source-hash marker for each remastered ISO
   321:       # The marker sibling stores the SOURCE hash; the decide step above compares
   322:       # it to re-remaster only when the pristine ISO is refreshed.
   323:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   324:         content: "{{ (_remaster_src.results | selectattr('item', 'equalto', item) | first).stat.checksum }}\n"
   325:         dest: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso.src.sha256"
   326:         mode: "0644"
   327:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   328:       loop_control:
   329:         label: "{{ item }}"
   330:       tags: [remaster]
   331: 
   332:     - name: World-readable perms on remastered ISOs (match the served dir)
   333:       ansible.builtin.file:
   334:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   335:         mode: "0644"
   336:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   337:       loop_control:
   338:         label: "{{ item }}"
   339:       tags: [remaster]
   340: 
   341:     - name: Compute sha256 of remastered ISOs
   342:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   343:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/{{ item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   344:         get_checksum: true
   345:         checksum_algorithm: sha256
   346:       register: _remaster_np_sha
   347:       loop: "{{ _to_remaster | default([]) }}"
   348:       loop_control:
   349:         label: "{{ item }}"
   350:       tags: [remaster]
   351: 
   352:     - name: Update SHA256SUMS with the remastered ISO hashes (idempotent by filename)
   353:       ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
   354:         path: "{{ _dst_dir }}/SHA256SUMS"
   355:         regexp: "  {{ (item.item[:-4] ~ '-noprompt.iso') | regex_escape }}$"
   356:         line: "{{ item.stat.checksum }}  {{ item.item[:-4] }}-noprompt.iso"
   357:         create: true
   358:         mode: "0644"
   359:       loop: "{{ _remaster_np_sha.results }}"
   360:       loop_control:
   361:         label: "{{ item.item }}"
   362:       tags: [remaster]
   363: 
   364:     - name: Remove the remaster scratch workspace
   365:       ansible.builtin.file:
   366:         path: "{{ _scratch }}"
   367:         state: absent
   368:       tags: [remaster]
